Its base class, `CaseInsensitiveMapping`, keeps each entry under its name in lower case beside the name as it was written, and has no method that changes it (`django/utils/datastructures.py:CaseInsensitiveMapping`).
That spelling is there for templates, where a hyphen cannot appear in a variable's name (`django/http/request.py:HttpHeaders.__getitem__`).

`HttpRequest.get_host` answers the question of which host the client asked for, and refuses to answer when the host is not one the site has agreed to serve (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest.get_host`).
It looks in up to three places, in a fixed order (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest._get_raw_host`).

A request with neither gets the server's own name from `"SERVER_NAME"`, with the port added when it is not the usual one for the scheme: `HttpRequest.get_port`'s answer, which is the `X-Forwarded-Port` header when `settings.USE_X_FORWARDED_PORT` is true and the request has one, and `"SERVER_PORT"` otherwise (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest.get_port`).

`validate_host` compares what is left with each pattern in the setting: `"*"` matches anything, a pattern that begins with a dot matches that domain and every subdomain of it, and any other pattern must be the host exactly (`django/http/request.py:split_domain_port`, `django/http/request.py:validate_host`, `django/utils/http.py:is_same_domain`).

An empty `ALLOWED_HOSTS` allows nothing, unless `settings.DEBUG` is true, when `get_host` uses in its place the local machine's names, `".localhost"`, `"127.0.0.1"` and `"[::1]"`, the first of which matches localhost and any subdomain of it (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest.get_host`).

That security release, with 1.9.11 and 1.8.16 beside it, checked the host in either case, and for convenience allowed the names of localhost when the setting was empty and debugging on (`docs/releases/1.10.3.txt`).
Subdomains of localhost, such as static.localhost, joined that fallback in 3.1 (`docs/releases/3.1.txt`).

Of the middleware that `django-admin startproject` writes, `CommonMiddleware.process_request` calls it for every request that gets past its check of `settings.DISALLOWED_USER_AGENTS` ([The general-purpose middleware](../handlers/general.md#commonmiddleware-on-the-way-in)), and `SecurityMiddleware.process_request`, listed before it, calls it when it redirects a request made over plain HTTP to HTTPS and `SECURE_SSL_HOST` is not set (`django/middleware/common.py:CommonMiddleware.process_request`, `django/middleware/security.py:SecurityMiddleware.process_request`).

Each item of the header becomes one `MediaType`, an item with a weight of zero is dropped, and a request with no such header is treated as accepting anything (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest.accepted_types`, `django/http/request.py:MediaType`).

`HttpRequest.accepted_types_by_precedence` is the same list sorted the other way, by how specific an item is first and by its weight second, and `HttpRequest.accepted_type` returns the first item of it that matches a given type (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest.accepted_type`).
`HttpRequest.accepts` says only whether a type is acceptable at all (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest.get_preferred_type`).
`get_preferred_type` was added in that release, and `accepted_types` has been sorted by the client's preference since then (`docs/releases/5.2.txt`).
